extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for the Journal of Fluid Mechanics using LaTeX and the JFM style file
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and formatting requirements for preparing JFM journal articles with the Cambridge University Press JFM LaTeX style (JFM.sty). Covers documentclass usage, macros, headings, math, figures, tables, theorem/proof environments, references, and production notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of JFM style file
rubrics_metrics.description: The JFM document style is implemented as a complete document style, not a document style option. Replace \documentstyle{article} by \documentstyle{JFM}. First, copy the file "JFM.sty" into the correct subdirectory on your system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of the standard document style options should be used. Once you have used the additional JFM facilities in your document, it can be processed only with JFM.sty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbidden/unsupported standard documentstyle options
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard document style options should not be used with the JFM style: 10pt, 11pt, 12pt (unavailable); draft, twoside (no associated style file) -- twoside is default; fleqn, leqno, titlepage, twocolumn -- unavailable; proc, ifthen, bezier -- can be used if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pass these options to \documentstyle when using JFM.sty; be aware which are explicitly unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-defined macros placement and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Author-defined macros should be inserted before \begin{document}, or in a separate file and should be included with the submission. Authors must not change any of the macro definitions or parameters in JFM.sty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather macros in the preamble or in a macros.tex included via \include{macros}. Do not scatter definitions through the document; mark font-replacement points with comments such as "% replace font!" so typesetter can substitute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running headlines (title and author short forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title and author's name are used both at the beginning of the article and throughout as running headlines: title on odd-numbered pages and author's name (initials only for first names) on even-numbered pages. The running headline must be a single line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the extended \title[<short title>]{...} and \author[<short author>]{...} forms to provide the short versions for running headlines. Do not use \pagestyle, \thispagestyle, \markright, or \markboth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and author-name formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The affiliation must be entered using \affiliation (do not use \\ in \author to start an affiliation). The \and command in \author only generates the word 'and' in small caps. Use \ls to letter-space author's names and \ns to insert space between author's names. For multiple affiliations, use \\[\affilskip] between lines and insert footnote numbers manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given in guide shows how to produce names, affiliations and received date. Use \thanks for footnotes at bottom of title page if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should appear just before the first \section command, produced by \begin{abstract} ... \end{abstract}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the abstract before \section; the JFM style provides an abstract environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: List environments and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: JFM provides the standard list environments and an additional unnumbered list: enumerate (numbered lists), itemize (bulleted lists), description (labelled lists). The enumerate environment numbers items with an italic letter in parentheses by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can redefine numbering (e.g., roman numerals) by redefining \theenumi after \begin{enumerate}. Use the optional argument to \begin{enumerate} to specify the widest label (e.g., \begin{enumerate}[(iii)]) to get correct alignment; once used, do not process with a standard LaTeX style file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof environment behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: A proof environment is provided: \begin{proof} ... \end{proof} prints a terminating proofbox; \begin{proof*} ... \end{proof*} omits the final proofbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the proof environment after theorem/lemma statements; examples illustrate usage and produced layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks/Notes/Problems formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarks, Notes, Problems, Comments, and Cases are typeset like proofs but without the closing proofbox. Use the \newremark command to define remark-like environments; for example \newremark{note}{Note} then \begin{note} ... \end{note}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works like \newtheorem but with no optional argument for numbering; text is typeset with an italic heading and roman text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed mathematics spacing and commands
rubrics_metrics.description: JFM style will insert correct space above and below displayed maths if standard LaTeX commands are used. Use \[ ... \] and not $$ ... $$. Do not leave blank lines above and below displayed equations unless a new paragraph is intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard LaTeX display-math conventions to get correct spacing in JFM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbering: subequations and subeqnarray
rubrics_metrics.description: The subequations and subeqnarray environments have been incorporated to allow numbering such as (6.1a), (6.1b) etc. In some NFSS cases there are caveats; alternatives using manual \eqno and \stepcounter{equation} are shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to use subequations/subeqnarray or, when NFSS issues occur, how to emulate the style with manual \eqno and careful spacing/alignment code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of multi-line equation arrays
rubrics_metrics.description: To align equals signs and make left- and right-hand sides the same width, authors may use width-measuring commands (\settowidth etc.) and manual spacing adjustments when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guide includes a full code example using \newlength, \settowidth, \advance, \vspace and manual \eqno placements to align multline arrays when subeqnarray doesn't produce desired alignment under NFSS.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS fonts: fallback and typesetter substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need AMS symbols but do not have the AMS fonts, set up user-defined macros that can be redefined by the typesetter (e.g., \def\BbbE{\mbox{\sf E}}). Ensure AMS fonts are at least version 2.1; submit your copy of mssymb.tex with your input file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define macros for symbols that the typesetter can replace. Plain TeX provides only \geq and \leq; these will be redefined at typesetting to use AMS macros. If using AMS Euler fonts include appropriate font definitions in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman, multiletter italic, and upright Greek symbol conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical operators/constants (sin, cos, log, exp) have macros to ensure roman type. For single-letter roman characters in math use \mathrm, e.g. $E=m\mathrm c^2$. For multiletter symbols use \mbox or define macros (e.g., \def\Real{\mbox{Re}}, \def\Rey{\mbox{\it Re}}). Define \upi and \umu for upright pi and mu so typesetter can substitute upright characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these macros instead of relying on AMS fonts; include their definitions in the preamble so typesetter can map to journal typeface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sans serif and bold-slanted symbol handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When bold-sloping sans serifs are needed, define macros (e.g., \def\ssC{\mbox{\sf C}}, \def\sfsP{\mbox{\sfs P}}, \def\slsQ{\mbox{\sls Q}}) and include font definitions that the typesetter will replace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer Modern lacks bold-slanted maths sans serif; the guide shows how to produce a proof copy that will be replaced by the typesetter's fonts later. Mark such places with comments so typesetter can substitute appropriate fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Script characters should be typeset using plain TeX's \mathcal command (e.g., \mathcal E, \mathcal F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typesetter will substitute the more florid script characters normally seen in the journal; using \mathcal in the input makes substitution straightforward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skewing of accents
rubrics_metrics.description: When accents over italic or sloping letters need to be shifted, use \skew, e.g. \def\hatp{\skew5\hat{p}} to center the accent correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define such macros in the preamble so accents are adjusted uniformly; example provided for \hatp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of measure formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers and their units should be typeset with fixed spaces that will not break over two lines. Use user-defined macros, e.g., \def\dynpercm{\nobreak\mbox{$\;$dynes\,cm$^{-1}$}} and then write 52\dynpercm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always keep number and unit together with non-breaking space constructs; provide macros in preamble for typesetter substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro name conflicts and checking
rubrics_metrics.description: If you define macros, ensure their names do not conflict with existing macros in plain TeX, LaTeX, or AMSTeX. Place them in the preamble. You can check whether a macro name is used by running TeX interactively and issuing \show\<macro_name> (or inserting \show into the preamble).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show \show\Re producing TeX's response; ensure user-defined names such as \Real are undefined before assignment. Keep macros where typesetter can find and modify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectioning levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the first three LaTeX section levels are defined in the JFM style: \begin{section} (Heading A), \begin{subsection} (Heading B), \begin{subsubsection} (Heading C). There is no paragraph or subparagraph in JFM style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain non-bold material in a bold heading, use plain TeX commands for changing typeface (example: \section{Fluctuations in Ca{\sc ii}}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table environment and caption placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the table environment for floating tables. Table captions should appear at the bottom of the table (place \caption after the body). The JFM \table command will insert rules above and below the table as required; do not insert rules yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not normally use positional qualifiers t, b, h on table environment. Vertical rules should never be used within table body; horizontal rules only to span columns with same headings. If two tables fall one above another, add \norule to the upper table and \followon between tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular modifications and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The tabular environment has been modified: additional vertical space is inserted above/below \hline; tables are centred and span full page width. Commands to redefine quantities such as \arraystretch should be omitted. If old tabular facilities are needed, use environment oldtabular which has none of the reformatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use minipage if table includes table footnotes. Examples show typical tabular usage for JFM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure handling and artwork submission
rubrics_metrics.description: At present figures cannot be handled using PostScript or similar files; artwork must be supplied separately as hard copy to be lettered and sized by the Printer. Leave approximate space using \vspace. Figure captions should be below the figure; place \caption after the space left for the illustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not normally use positional qualifiers t, b, h on figure environment; JFM style handles figure placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem-like environment creation and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: No theorem-like environments are predefined in JFM.sty; authors must define each using \newtheorem (Theorem, Definition, Lemma, Corollary, Proposition). Preferred numbering is within sections (1.1, 1.2...), but other schemes are permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide \newtheorem declarations in the preamble. Example: \newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}[section] and optional redefinitions of numbering style via \renewcommand{\thelemma}{...}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments should appear at the close of your paper, just before the list of references and any appendices. Use the acknowledgments environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The environment simply inserts appropriate vertical space; place it before references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix usage and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the standard LaTeX \appendix command to place appendices, normally just before the references. This numbers appendices as A, B etc., equations as (A1), (B1), and figures/tables as A1, B1 etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices should be placed before the references unless production requires otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting and citation style
rubrics_metrics.description: References can be produced by a thebibliography environment or by BibTeX. References in the text are given by author and date (e.g., \cite{Den85}). Each \bibitem should take the form \bibitem[Author(s) (Date)]{tag} Bibliography entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author(s) should appear as cited in text, Date is the date to be cited, and tag is the key used with \cite. Examples of formatted bibliography entries are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of special commands and environments to use
rubrics_metrics.description:
Appendix summarizes new commands, optional arguments and environments added to standard LaTeX in JFM.sty (e.g., \affiliation, \affilskip,  ollowon, \ls, 
ewremark, 
orule, 
s; optional args: [<short title>] in 	itle, [<short author>] in \author, [<widest label>] in  egin{enumerate}; new environments: proof, proof*, remark, subeqnarray, subequation, modified tabular).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should review this table to find the exact commands and environments they are expected to use in JFM submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production/editorial notes to check
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes for editors include catchline commands to be placed in the preamble (\pubyear{}, \volume{}, \pagerange{}), checking footnote placement, rules between tables (use \norule and \followon), font substitution and font sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors need not worry about some production details (fonts, final catchlines) but should supply macros and mark replacements so editors/typesetters can do final production. Check for AMS fonts, bold slanted sans serifs and bold math italic usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font-size definitions and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: JFM style defines the standard LaTeX font sizes and some special sizes (e.g., \indexsize, \qsmall). Table lists sizes, baseline, and intended usage (e.g., \normalsize = main text, abstract, B and C heads; \LARGE = article title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided size-changing commands as intended; do not invent custom font-size manipulations expecting the same output in the journal typeface.
